questions.question: In the context of Mughal administration, which of the following is the most appropriate definition of 'Abwab'?

options.text: A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent
A clerk in the government treasury

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• ** Abwab**__

• All irregular impositions on** RAIYATS** above the established assessment of land in the PARGANA.
 
• Land tax was established by **Todar Mal **after a field-to-survey.

questions.question: Whose administration became a model that was followed by Akbar when he consolidated the Mughal Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sher Shah Suri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Akbar** **followed **the **administration model **of **Sher Shah Suri**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sher Shah Suri** was the **founder **of the **Suri Empire **in **India**.

 
 
• He **introduced **the **currency **of the **Rupee**.
 
• Sher Shah of Sur took **control **of the **Mughal Empire **in **1540**.
 
• His **reorganization **of the **empire **laid the **foundations **for the** later Mughal emperors**, **notably Akbar**, son of Humayun.
 
 
 
• **Sher Shah Suri's administration**:
 
 
• He organized an **excellent administrative system**.
 
• The king was aided by** four important ministers**.
 
 
• **Diwan –i- Wizarat **or **Wazir **– in charge of Revenue and Finance
 
• **Diwan-i-Ariz** – in charge of Army
 
• **Diwan-i-Rasalat** – Foreign Minister
 
• **Diwan-i-Insha** – Minister for Communications
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__ **

 
• Akbar (1542- 1605)

 
 
• He reigned from 1556 to 1605.
 
• He defeated Hemu at the second battle of Panipat in 1556.
 
• He constructed Fatehpur Sikri and made it his capital in 1569.
 
• He started a new religion Din-i Ilahi in 1582.
 
• Abul Fazl wrote his biography titled Akbarnama.
 
• Nine of his courtiers were known as Navratnas.
 
 
• They were Todar Mal, Abul Fazal, Faizi, Birbal, Tansen, Abdur Rahim Khana-i-Khana, Mullah-do-Pyaza, Raja Man Singh, and Fakir Aziao-Din.
 
 
 
• He married a Hindu princess Harka Bai who was commonly known as Jodha Bhai
 
• Akbar captured the historic fortress of Chitor in 1568.
 
• He abolished the pilgrimage tax by Hindus in 1563.
 
• He abolished the Jizyah tax in 1564.
 
• He also introduced the Mansabdari System or the rank-holder system to organize the nobility and army.

questions.question: Which Mughal prince translated the Upanishads into Persian in 1657?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dara Shikoh.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Dara Shikoh translated 50 Upanishads from Sanskrit to Persian so they could be read by Muslim scholars.
 
• His translation is often called Sirr-i-Akbar.
 
• Dara Shikoh was the eldest son and heir apparent of the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• He devoted much effort towards finding a common mystical language between Islam and Hinduism.
 
• His spiritual quest for monotheistic strands in Hindu philosophy was a continuous process.
 
• This led him to study the Upanishads, with the help of some scholars of Benaras.
 
• This book was the greatest mystery and was completed in 1657.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other important translations:

 
 
• Ramayana and Singhasan Batisi were translated by Mulla Abdul Qadir Badayuni into Persian.
 
• Panchatantra was translated into Persian by Faizi.
 
• Rajataringini was translated by Maulana Shah Mohammad Shahabadi.
 
• Abul Fazl wrote the Ain-i-Akbari and Akbar Nama.

questions.question: Mughal Emperor ______ permitted the English East India Company to establish their factory in 1613 at Surat.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is__** Jahangir**__.

__
 
• Mughal Emperor Jahangir permitted the English East India Company to establish their factory in 1613 at Surat.
 
• 
 The British East India Company came to India for trading in spices, an important commodity in Europe back then and as it was used to preserve meat.
 
 
• Apart from this, they primarily do trading in silk, cotton, indigo dye, tea, and opium.
 
• Mughal emperor **Jahangir granted** a Farman to **Captain William Hawkins** permitting the **English to erect a factory at Surat in 1613. **
 
• In** 1615, Thomas Roe, the Ambassador to James I**, got an imperial Farman from Jahangir for doing trading and **establish factories all across the Mughal empire.**
 
• In **1616**, the **company established its first factory** in the** south in Masulipattanam.**
 
• Soon, the **Vijaynagara Empire will also give the company permission** to open a **factory in Madras **and the **British company** started to eclipse out the other European trading companies in their rising power.
 
• The 'East India Company' was formed in 1600.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Akbar called him **Sheik Babu.**
 
• After his coronation, he assumed the title of** Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir Badshah Ghazi.**
 
• Jahangir was the only surviving son of Akbar who after his **father’s death ascended the throne in 1604, at the age of 34 years. **

questions.question: Aurangzeb ruled the Mughal empire from ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is from __**1658 to 1707 AD**__.

__
 
• **Aurangzeb ruled the Mughal empire from 1658 to 1707 AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aurangzeb (1658 AD-1707 AD):**

 
 
• Aurangzeb defeated Dara at Dharmat (1658 AD), Samugarh (1658 AD), and Deorai, in which Samugarh was the decisive one and Deorai was the last one.
 
• After the victory, Aurangzeb was crowned at Delhi under the title ***Alamgir***. He **died in February 1707 **in **Ahmadnagar**.
 
• Aurangzeb captured **Guru Teg Bahadur**, the 9th Guru of Sikhs in 1675 AD and executed him when he refused to embrace Islam.
 
 
• The **10th and last Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh**, son of Guru Teg Bahadur, organized his followers into a community of warriors called ***Khalsa*** to fight against the Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj** was the most powerful Maratha king and an arch-enemy of Aurangzeb.
 
• The Mughal conquests reached a climax during Aurangzeb’s reign as **Bijapur **and **Golconda **were annexed in **1686 AD and 1687 AD**, respectively.
 
• Under him, the Mughal empire reached its greatest extent and the largest single-state ever known in India.
 
• He forbade the inscription of ***Kalma ***on the coins, also forbade **sati and Jharokha-darshan**.
 
• He** ended the celebration of Navroz** and, in 1679 AD, **reimposed Jizya. **
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Aurangzeb was initiated into the** Naqshbandiya order.**
 
• The only monument associated with Aurangzeb is ***Bibi ka Maqbara***, which is the tomb of his wife **Rabbia-ud-Daura, in Aurangabad.**

questions.question: In the context of economic system of Mughal Empire, the term 'Polaj' referred to ______.

options.text: a type of coin introduced by Akbar

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "__**annually cultivated land**__".​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the Mughal Period, the land was divided into four categories namely
 
 
• Polaj.
 
• Parati.
 
• Chachar.
 
• Banjar.
 
 
 
• Polaj was the land that is annually cultivated for each crop in succession and is never allowed to lie fallow.
 
• Polaj was the ideal and best type of land throughout the empire.
 
• This land was cultivated always and was never allowed to lie fallow. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• There was no **Mughal land revenue system **before **Akbar**.
 
• His father Humayun and grandfather Babur did not introduce any changes because they were the first conquerors of their dynasty and remained pre-occupied with subduing rebellions, consolidating empires, and maintaining order.
 
• A prope**r land revenue system **was founded by **Akbar**.
 
• However, the system of Akbar was itself based on what **Shershah Suri **implemented during his short tenure.
 
• Thus, the land revenue system of Akbar was neither innovation nor an invention.
 
• His indebtedness to the earlier rulers is immense but this has not diminished his fame as far as **the land revenue system **is concerned.
 
• He followed the policy of **Shershah** with greater precision and correctness and then extended it to various subah or provinces of his empire.
 
• But this correction or precision did not come overnight.
 
• Initially was tortuous enough to turn peasants into **beggars**, and forcing them to **sell their wives and children.**
 
• But it was revised several times.

**The corrections done by the Akbar inland revenue system can be mainly divided into three heads as follows:**

 
• Standardization of measurement of land
 
• Ascertaining the produce per Bigha of Land
 
• Fixation of state’s share in that produce

questions.question: Which of the following places is associated with the tomb of Jahangir?

__

• He is known for his strict administration of justice.
 
• He established **Zanjir-i-Adil (chain of justice) at Agra **for the seekers of royal justice.
 
• He was the **eldest son of Akbar** was born at** Fatehpur Sikri near Agra in 1569.**
 
• In 1611, he married **Mehr-un-Nisa** whom he gave the title of **Nur Jahan (light of the world).**
 
• He defeated and imprisoned his son, Khusrau Mirza.
 
• He also beheaded **Guru Arjun**, the 5th Sikh Guru and one of the supporters of Khusrau Mirza.
 
• **Captain Hawkins (1608-1611) and Sir Thomas Roe (1615-1616) **visited Jahangir's court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Dara Shikoh** had been given the title of **‘Sultan Buland Iqbal’** or **Shahzada-e-Buland Iqba** by **Shah Jahan**.
 
• **Dara Shikoh** was the eldest son of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• Shah Jahan declared Dara Shikoh as his successor.
 
• He was appointed as** Governor of Multan and Kabul** in **1652**.
 
• In the war of succession, **Dara Shikoh** was defeated by **Aurangzeb** and **executed in 1659** on his order.
 
• Dara Shikoh was known to be Intellectual, liberal, and Sufi.
 
• Some of his literary works are **Tariqat ul-Haqiqat, Iksir-i Azam, Risaala-i Haq Numa, Sirr-e-Akbar** etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There were four sons of Shah Jahan namely,
 
 
• Dara Shikoh
 
• Shah Suja
 
• Murad
 
• Aurangzeb
 
 
 
• The war of succession was fought between the sons of Shah Jahan.
 
• Although, Shah Jahan declared **Dara Shikoh** as his successor, ultimately Aurangzeb won the war of succession and declared himself the king.
 
• **In 1659**, in the **battle of Deorai,** **Aurangzeb **defeated **Dara Shikoh** and executed him.
